edges.description: Loss of hydratase activity blocks leucine catabolism, diverting upstream intermediates into abnormally excreted organic acids.
Over years to decades the disorder manifests as a progressive white-matter disease; the mechanistic connection between the accumulating organic acids and CNS injury is unresolved.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in AUH reduce or abolish mitochondrial 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA hydratase activity. This enzyme catalyzes the conversion of 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA to 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA (HMG-CoA) within the leucine degradation pathway — the leucine-catabolic step that had remained the last to be characterized at the enzyme and DNA level until AUH was identified as its gene.

evidence.reference_title: 3-Methylglutaconic aciduria type I is caused by mutations in AUH.
evidence.snippet: This disorder is caused by a deficiency of 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA hydratase, one of the key enzymes of leucine degradation.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic heterogeneity in two siblings with 3-methylglutaconic aciduria type I caused by a novel intragenic deletion.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis was confirmed by a demonstration of 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA hydratase enzyme deficiency in the cultured skin fibroblasts and homozygous deletion of exons 1-3 within the AUH gene.

nodes.description: The metabolic block causes accumulation and excessive urinary excretion of 3-methylglutaconic acid, 3-methylglutaric acid, and 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid — the abnormal organic-acid profile that is the biochemical hallmark of MGA1. Unlike the classic intoxication-type organic acidemias, the accumulating acids are not associated with recurrent acute acidotic/hyperammonemic crises, and their neurotoxic potential is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Biochemical characterization of human 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA hydratase and its role in leucine metabolism.
evidence.snippet: The metabolic disease 3-methylglutaconic aciduria type I (MGA1) is characterized by an abnormal organic acid profile in which there is excessive urinary excretion of 3-methylglutaconic acid, 3-methylglutaric acid and 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid.

nodes.description: MGA1 is redefined as a slowly progressive leukoencephalopathy. Adult patients present with a highly characteristic clinical and neuroradiologic pattern — progressive ataxia, spasticity, optic atrophy, and dementia with extensive cerebral white-matter disease on MRI — whereas childhood presentation is nonspecific (delayed speech, learning problems) or absent. White-matter abnormalities may already begin in the first decades of life. This node is intentionally NOT declared to conform to the module's acute "Metabolic Decompensation"/"Acute Metabolic Encephalopathy" nodes, because MGA1 lacks the acute catabolic-crisis pattern of the classic intoxication-type organic acidemias.
